channel.title: Updated · all tabs
channel.description: Daily news and research, explained: every tab

item.title: Independent interferometric observable confirms black hole shadow in M87*
item.description: An independent imaging method built only on calibration-proof measurements recovers the ring around M87's black hole, 42.2 microarcseconds across, implying a mass of about 6.5 billion Suns. (Samuel Lai, Nithyanandan Thyagarajan, O. Ivy Wong et al.)

item.title: Hadean mantle depletion and 3.95-Gyr subduction implied by North China rocks
item.description: A newly found 3.95-billion-year-old rock in North China formed from ocean crust buried to mantle depths, suggesting a short-lived subduction event early in Earth's history. (Hangqiang Xie, Chunyan Dong, Pengchuan Li et al.)

item.title: Flexible rubber blades for tidal turbines
item.description: Tidal turbine blades made of flexible rubber matched the energy yield of rigid blades with active pitch control while cutting fatigue-causing load swings by up to a third. (Zhehong Zhang, Junchen Tan, Eric-Carin Neba et al.)

item.title: Jensen Huang resigns as Nvidia's CEO, CFO Colette Kress takes over on an interim basis, and the shares open down more than 13%
item.description: Nvidia's co-founder Jensen Huang resigned as CEO and director with immediate effect; CFO Colette Kress is interim CEO while the board searches for a successor, and Huang has agreed to testify to Congress. (TechCrunch, BBC, TechCrunch)

item.title: The Fed scraps its October 2027 rate vote and holds no December meeting, so no rate decision is due between mid-November 2027 and late January 2028
item.description: The Fed's revised 2027 calendar keeps eight meetings but turns October's into a strategy session with no rate decision and drops December, part of Chair Kevin Warsh's plan to meet less often. (Federal Reserve, The New York Times)

item.title: US existing-home sales fall 5.5% in October to 3.75 million, the lowest pace since August 2010, as mortgage rates climb
item.description: Sales of previously owned US homes fell 5.5% in October to an annual pace of 3.75 million, down 8.8% from a year earlier, as 30-year mortgage rates hover near 7.18%. (National Association of Realtors, The Guardian)

item.title: Cisco raises its annual revenue forecast to as much as $75.8 billion after a record quarter driven by AI networking
item.description: Cisco's quarterly revenue rose 24% to a record $18.5 billion, beating estimates, and it lifted its fiscal 2027 outlook and its forecast for AI infrastructure sales to cloud giants to $9 billion. (Cisco, The Globe and Mail)

item.title: Clearing the Fog: Price Transparency, Market Churn, and Consumer Welfare in Short-Term Rentals
item.description: After California required Airbnb and similar hosts to show fee-inclusive prices, guests became more price-sensitive, nightly rates rose 4.8%, and many fee-heavy listings left the market, with net gains for consumers on average. (Ginger Zhe Jin, Liad Wagman, Jingyi Xing)

item.title: Google launches Gemini 4 Hydrogen, a fast Gemini 4 model that replaces 3.8 Flash and now powers Search
item.description: Google released Gemini 4 Hydrogen, a fast, cheaper Gemini 4 model priced at $1.50/$7.50 per million tokens that scores level with the frontier Argon model on one index and now runs Google Search. (Google DeepMind, Ars Technica, TechCrunch)

item.title: Nonprofits sue OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Meta and SpaceX to halt frontier AI development
item.description: Four nonprofits asked a San Francisco court to stop five leading AI developers from building or deploying new models, citing the companies' own warnings of catastrophic risk under California unfair-competition law. (Associated Press via BNN Bloomberg, Reuters via Claims Journal)

item.title: Goal Encoding in LLMs
item.description: A sparse set of attention heads in a coding LLM encodes the next sub-goal before it is written, can be read out in plain English, and steers behavior across programming languages. (Arnab Sen Sharma, Eric Todd, Sheridan Feucht et al. · Northeastern University, Parallax, University of Copenhagen)

item.title: Is Your Robot's Memory Just a Clock? Temporal Shortcuts in Memory-Augmented VLA Policies
item.description: Memory-augmented robot policies often track elapsed time rather than events, so a harmless pause makes them believe work was done; indexing memory by events recovers much of the loss. (Chubin Zhang, Bo An · Nanyang Technological University)

item.title: Factored One-sided Adam-Moment for Practical and Scalable SOAP
item.description: FOAM keeps nearly all of the SOAP optimizer's quality in LLM pre-training while using half its optimizer memory and reaching AdamW's final loss in about AdamW's own wall-clock time. (Jaemyung Yu, Byeongho Heo, Sangdoo Yun et al. · NAVER AI Lab)

item.title: Tree-Ising: Repairing Language Models with Bit-Level Ising Edits
item.description: Tree-Ising fixes a small reasoning model's endless loops by flipping signs and shifting exponents in its stored weights, beating a frontier-agent repair on math benchmarks at about $0.90 instead of $312. (Hadi Salloum, Ammar Ali)

item.title: Actor, Judge, or Teacher? Understanding Decision Models in Long-Horizon Agents
item.description: Decision models that act poorly can still teach well: asked in hindsight whether each action helped, JEV lifts a 1.5B agent's ALFWorld success from 72.8% to 82.9% over outcome-only GRPO. (Haochen Liu, Qianhao Zhu, Zixuan Wang et al. · Zhejiang University, Baidu Inc.)

item.title: A Microsoft 365 outage tied to Exchange Online knocks out email, Teams and Copilot for more than 12 hours
item.description: Microsoft 365 services that depend on Exchange Online failed worldwide from Thursday afternoon, and Microsoft's fixes had not brought sustained recovery more than 12 hours later. (BleepingComputer, The Register)

item.title: Apache patches a critical HTTP/2 flaw in its web server that could let attackers run code remotely
item.description: Apache HTTP Server 2.4.71 fixes a critical race condition in its HTTP/2 module that could let an unauthenticated attacker run code on servers that have HTTP/2 switched on. (Apache HTTP Server Project, BleepingComputer)

item.title: Police in nine countries seize 235 servers behind the Gootloader, CastleRAT and StealC malware
item.description: An Operation Endgame action coordinated by Europol took down 235 servers and 257 domains used by three malware families and found about 6.4 million stolen credentials. (BleepingComputer, The Record)

item.title: Google opens pre-orders for its first Gemini smart glasses, made with Warby Parker, Gentle Monster and Samsung
item.description: Google's camera-equipped "intelligent eyewear," starting at $395, is up for pre-order ahead of a December 10 launch, with privacy limits such as a tamper-checked recording light. (Google, Ars Technica)

item.title: A Universal Fault-Tolerant Quantum Computing Architecture with Globally Driven Atom Arrays
item.description: A design for neutral-atom quantum computers that picks which qubits to operate on by moving helper atoms, letting simple global laser and microwave pulses run error-corrected computation in simulation. (Zhihao Zhang, Shuaifan Cao, Xinyang Yu et al. · Fudan University)

item.title: Beam's base-edited sickle cell therapy keeps patients free of severe pain crises for a year in its pivotal trial
item.description: Beam Therapeutics says its one-time base-edited cell therapy, risto-cel, met its main goal of 12 months without severe pain crises in a 49-patient single-arm trial, and plans a US filing. (PharmaShots (summary of Beam's press release), BioPharm International)

item.title: A Lancet Psychiatry analysis compares how well 21 antidepressants keep depression at bay over months to years
item.description: Pooling 115 studies longer than 12 weeks, researchers found escitalopram, duloxetine and agomelatine somewhat more likely than fluoxetine to bring lasting improvement; experts call the differences modest. (The New York Times, BBC News)

item.title: Everyone in a 100,000-person All of Us sample carries gene variants that affect medicines, and a quarter got an affected drug
item.description: A Pitt-led analysis of nearly 100,000 genomes found every participant carried at least one drug-relevant variant (median nine), 24.4% had been prescribed an affected drug, and over 17,000 variants were new. (University of Pittsburgh via Medical Xpress, STAT, Science Translational Medicine)

item.title: UNC13A splice correction rescues synaptic dysfunction induced by TDP-43 loss
item.description: In lab-grown human neurons lacking the ALS protein TDP-43, fixing one splicing error in the synapse gene UNC13A with an antisense drug restored communication between neurons. (Matthew J. Keuss, Peter Harley, Eugeni Ryadnov et al. · King's College London; University College London; Francis Crick Institute; Leibniz-FMP; Trace Neuroscience)

item.title: Evolutionary dynamics in the years preceding acute myeloid leukaemia
item.description: Yearly stored blood samples show that in two-thirds of women who later got acute myeloid leukaemia, the first driver mutation arose before age 20, and mutant clones then grew predictably. (Caroline J. Watson, Gladys Y. P. Poon, Hamish A. J. MacGregor et al. · University of Cambridge; University College London)

item.title: Human land use drives microplastic abundance in terrestrial wildlife
item.description: GPS-tracked tapirs and giant anteaters in Brazil carried more microplastics in their blood when their home ranges held more human disturbance or lay nearer waste facilities. (Marcia de Almeida Monteiro Melo Ferraz, Arnaud L. J. Desbiez, Mario Henrique Alves et al. · University of British Columbia (Kelowna); Center for Advanced Systems Understanding (CASUS), Helmholtz-Zentrum Dresden-Rossendorf)

item.title: Euclid's first major data release maps more than 900 million galaxies and about 15,000 likely gravitational lenses
item.description: ESA's Euclid telescope has published its first major data release, covering about 14% of its planned survey, with over 900 million galaxies, 60 million possible quasars and roughly 15,000 probable strong lenses. (The Guardian, ESA Euclid)

item.title: ESA's Hera begins close-up study of the asteroid pair NASA's DART mission hit in 2022
item.description: ESA says its Hera spacecraft is now studying the asteroid Didymos and its moonlet Dimorphos from 25 to 30 kilometres away, starting a "crash site investigation" of the first asteroid deflection test. (Phys.org (Associated Press), ESA)

item.title: The two most notorious "forever chemicals" have fallen by about 30% in England's rivers, but replacements are appearing
item.description: An Environment Agency report finds PFOS and PFOA concentrations in English rivers fell 30% and 29% over a decade, while short-chain substitutes such as trifluoroacetic acid are now widespread. (New Scientist, BBC News)

item.title: Bound states in the continuum through quantum interference in ultracold atomic collisions
item.description: Physicists created a molecular state of two lithium atoms that stays bound above the energy at which it should fall apart, by making two collision resonances cancel each other's escape routes. (Alexander Guthmann, Louisa Marie Kienesberger, Felix Lang et al.)

item.title: Majorana edge reconstruction and the ν = 5/2 non-Abelian thermal Hall puzzle
item.description: Theorists propose that the edge of the 5/2 quantum Hall state reorganises itself into stripes, which would reconcile a long-running clash between heat-flow experiments and numerical predictions. (Tevž LotričTaige WangMichael P. ZaletelSteven H. SimonS. A. ParameswaranaRudolf Peierls Centre for Theoretical Physics, Oxford OX1 3PU, United Kingdombhttps://ror.org/01an7q238Department of Physics et al. · Rudolf Peierls Centre for Theoretical Physics, University of Oxford; Department of Physics, University of California at Berkeley)

item.title: Nvidia's board prepares to replace CEO Jensen Huang, and the stock falls about 8% after hours
item.description: Nvidia's board met to prepare for removing co-founder and CEO Jensen Huang after two reported affairs, one with a suspected Chinese spy; the shares fell about 8% in after-hours trading. (TechCrunch, Fortune, The Globe and Mail)

item.title: UK economy grows 0.7% in the third quarter, its fastest pace in more than two years
item.description: UK GDP rose 0.7% from July to September, led by services such as computer programming tied to cloud and AI spending, despite higher energy prices from the Iran war. (Office for National Statistics, BBC)

item.title: EU court adviser says Google's annulled 1.49 billion euro AdSense fine was wrongly scrapped
item.description: Advocate General Juliane Kokott told the EU's top court that a lower court erred in 2024 when it annulled Google's AdSense fine, and proposed sending the case back for a new ruling. (TNW, EU Law Live)

item.title: Canadian Tire beats profit estimates as higher gas prices lift sales, and raises its dividend
item.description: Canadian Tire's third-quarter profit rose to $246.4 million, beating forecasts, as pricier gasoline boosted sales; comparable sales rose 4.4%, or 1.7% without its gas business. (The Globe and Mail, Canadian Tire Corporation (newswire))

item.title: The Main Monetary Policy Shock
item.description: Combining three kinds of Fed announcement surprises, the authors find monetary policy shocks explain about 18% of swings in consumer prices over four years, far more than prior work suggested. (Christoph Boehm, Husang Kim, T. Niklas Kroner · University of Texas at Austin, Federal Reserve Board of Governors)

item.title: Google DeepMind releases AlphaGenome 2, which predicts how DNA variants act in specific cell types
item.description: AlphaGenome 2 predicts how DNA changes alter gene activity in individual cell types and states, finding nearly twice as many causal variants as its predecessor; it is open for non-commercial research. (Google DeepMind, The Verge)

item.title: Google launches the Gemini Decisions API, a model that scores yes/no, choice and rubric questions in one pass
item.description: Gemini Decision 1 answers up to 1,000 closed-set questions about a multimodal input in one forward pass, returning calibrated probabilities in 150-250 ms for $0.10 per million input tokens and no output charge. (Google, Simon Willison)

item.title: The Surprising Effectiveness of Deleting Weights in LLM Post-Training
item.description: Learning which 0.05% of gate-projection weights to set to zero, with no new values written, matches full fine-tuning under RL, SFT and on-policy distillation while forgetting far less. (Jack Lu, Zhenbang Yang, Mike Lasby et al. · New York University, University of Calgary)

item.title: Are Dense Rewards Worth Their Tokens in GRPO?
item.description: Across 1,668 preregistered runs, dense step-level rewards that beat GRPO per update lose once their extra generated tokens and GPU time are counted, while picking prompts near 50% success holds up. (Vikash Singh, Weicong Chen, Debargha Ganguly et al.)

item.title: Don't Just Trust Your Memory: Evidence-Linked Memory Reduces Memory-Induced Degradation in LLM Agents
item.description: WikiTrace links each lesson in an agent's memory to the run it came from, so the agent can check doubtful lessons, raising scores on all eight test suites and cutting memory-induced failures. (Yukyeong Lee, Yumin Choi, Jinheon Baek et al. · KAIST, DeepAuto.ai)

item.title: Evolving Infra: Agent-Adaptive LLM Serving at Scale
item.description: Evolving Infra lets serving nodes switch between prefill and decode in seconds and evicts cached context that no live agent branch needs, cutting latency up to 4.1x versus NVIDIA's Dynamo. (Hao Kang, Weili Xu, Ziyang Li et al.)

item.title: World In-Context Learning for Agentic Robot Manipulation
item.description: A frozen foundation model learns robot tasks by rehearsing in a simulator and writing lessons into a text memory, reaching 83.4% on RoboTwin 2.0 from one demonstration, over 20 points above trained policies. (Heng Fang, Zehui Guo, Yuehan Zhang et al. · Huazhong University of Science and Technology, ArcheOne AI)

item.title: Attackers push rogue remote-access clients to hundreds of PCs through managed service providers' ScreenConnect panels
item.description: Attackers used cloud-hosted ScreenConnect panels to install rogue remote-access software on at least 288 computers at 48 organizations; ConnectWise disabled five third-party extensions across about 400 partner environments. (BleepingComputer, Huntress)

item.title: Maersk confirms data theft from a legacy logistics system as a ransomware gang demands $5 million
item.description: Maersk says attackers stole data from an isolated system inherited through an acquisition; the WhiteArmor gang claims about 100GB and wants $5 million in bitcoin within 30 days. (BleepingComputer, The Register)

item.title: The EU proposes a Digital Fairness Act to ban dark patterns, rein in addictive design and limit loot boxes for minors
item.description: The European Commission's draft Digital Fairness Act would ban manipulative "dark patterns," let users switch off addictive features, curb pay-to-win games for minors and allow fines of up to 6% of global turnover. (The Verge, Engadget)

item.title: IBM's quantum roadmap swaps nine linked chips for two larger ones, targeting about 1,040 qubits in 2027
item.description: At its developer conference, IBM said its current Nighthawk r2 chip runs circuits of over 7,500 operations, and planned a 520-qubit Nighthawk r3 for 2027, with two chips linked into a roughly 1,040-qubit system. (IBM Quantum, Ars Technica)

item.title: Machine-learning decoders for fusion-based quantum computing in real time
item.description: PRISM, a transformer-based decoder for photonic quantum computers, matches slower integer-programming decoders on accuracy and runs on an AMD FPGA with 6.59-microsecond latency. (Daniel Barter, Jacob C. Bridgeman, Chris Dawson et al.)

item.title: Gemini and Webb find the oldest compact pair of quasars, two black holes that grew too big too early
item.description: Astronomers found two actively feeding supermassive black holes, 1.5 billion and 400 million solar masses, only 18,100 light-years apart just 900 million years after the Big Bang, the oldest compact quasar pair known. (NSF NOIRLab, Phys.org)

item.title: NASA studies show how the LISA observatory could find planets with gravitational waves
item.description: Two papers in The Astrophysical Journal work out how the planned LISA space observatory could detect giant planets orbiting pairs of white dwarfs, and how the Webb telescope could confirm them. (NASA)

item.title: A vanished chemical fingerprint dates the switch to modern-style plate tectonics to 2.5 billion years ago
item.description: Curtin University geologists found that a chemical signature of crust formed about 4 billion years ago appears in rocks worldwide until 2.5 billion years ago, then disappears, marking a shift towards large-scale crustal recycling. (Curtin University, Phys.org)

item.title: Ultrafast Meissner-levitated microrotor
item.description: A 30-micrometre magnet levitated above a superconductor at 4.2 K spins at 2.3 MHz, the fastest magnetically levitated rotor reported, with friction so low it serves as a pressure gauge and a dark-matter probe. (Joel K. Jose, Andrea Marchese, Marion Cromb et al.)

item.title: Photonic entanglement swapping with remote quantum dots
item.description: Physicists entangled two photons that never interacted by combining photon pairs from two separate on-demand quantum dots, reaching a swapping fidelity of 0.71, a step toward quantum repeaters built from deterministic light sources. (Mattia Beccaceci, Giuseppe Ronco, Fabrizio Cienzo et al. · Sapienza Università di Roma; Politecnico di Milano; Johannes Kepler University Linz; University of Würzburg; Paderborn University; Karlsruhe Institute of Technology)

item.title: Modified Newtonian Dynamics and galaxy clusters
item.description: Applied to 106 X-ray-mapped galaxy clusters, Modified Newtonian Dynamics cuts the needed unseen mass 4 to 10 times, leaving a compact residual that could be dark ordinary matter. (Francoise Combesahttps://ror.org/00cpdar66Observatoire de Paris, Laboratoire d’étude de l’Univers et des phénomènes eXtrêmes, Collège de France et al. · Observatoire de Paris; Collège de France; CNRS)

item.title: US consumer prices rise 0.4% in October, more than forecast, keeping a December Fed hike in play
item.description: The US consumer price index rose 0.4% in October, above the 0.3% analysts expected but slower than September's 0.6%, as energy price increases eased. (The Guardian, BBC News)

item.title: Bank of Canada notes show it hiked because energy costs were starting to spread, and it may go further
item.description: The Bank of Canada's summary of its October 28 deliberations shows officials raised the rate to 2.5% to stop high energy prices becoming broad inflation and did not rule out more hikes. (Bank of Canada)

item.title: Boeing to cut about 5% of its commercial airplane workforce as it slows its production ramp-up
item.description: Boeing will cut roughly 5% of its commercial airplane staff through layoffs and attrition after slowing plans to raise jet output, with layoff notices starting in December. (The Guardian, KIRO 7 News)

item.title: Children's Place files for bankruptcy and puts its kidswear brands up for sale
item.description: Children's Place, owner of the Gymboree brand, filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection and set a December 9 deadline for bids on its assets after falling sales and mounting losses. (The Globe and Mail, FashionUnited)

item.title: Unconventional Monetary Policy and Deposit Retention
item.description: Years of zero interest rates and Fed bond buying filled US banks with rate-sensitive depositors, which made keeping deposits costlier and riskier once rates rose in 2015 and 2022. (Philip Strahan, Tuo Yang · Boston College)

item.title: Google opens Gemini 4 Carbon to all paying developers and Ultra subscribers, with an agent "swarm" preview
item.description: Two weeks after a defenders-only debut, Google's strongest model, Gemini 4 Carbon, is available through the API and to AI Ultra subscribers at $2/$10 per million tokens, alongside a multi-agent "/swarm" preview. (Google DeepMind, The Verge)
